en: General Table of Contents for the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhao of Huaihai:
Tongzhou Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Temple;
Pingjiang Prefecture Shuangta Shouning Wansui Chan Temple.
Qingliang Guanghui Chan Temple in Jiankang Prefecture;
Wannian Baoen Guangxiao Chan Temple in Taizhou;
and Wanshou Baoen Guangxiao Chan Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture.
Longxiang Xingqing Chan Temple at Jiangxin Island, Wenzhou;
Guangli Chan Temple on Mount Ayuwang, Qingyuan Prefecture;
and Jingci Baoen Guangxiao Chan Temple in Lin’an Prefecture.
Eulogies for the Buddhas and Patriarchs of Lingyin Chan Temple (Jingde Era) and Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Temple at Mount Jing.
The Recorded Sayings of Master Huaihai of Tongzhou Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Temple,
compiled by his disciples Shi-ren, Zong-wen, Fa-qi, and Shou-yuan.
In the sixth year of the Shaoding era, on the third day of the tenth month, the Master was invited to enter the monastery at Daochang in Anji Prefecture.

Pointing to the Buddha Hall, he said, "I have spent three years rinsing my mouth with the word 'Buddha. Why is it that today we burn incense and prostrate together, shoulder to shoulder, in these monastic robes?"
Seated upon the square measure of the patriarch’s hall, a bright mirror faces the dais; both barbarian and Han appear therein. Earth turns and heaven revolves—where can they be met?

He lets out a shout. Taking up the official decree, he judges the void; a thousand words and ten thousand phrases all flow toward the source. Spiritually self-attained, a single hair [pervades it all].
A message is transmitted from head to head. If your seeing and hearing have not yet been extinguished, listen to what follows.
Pointing to the Dharma seat: "Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one is always within it. Why then, today, do you treat it with such particular solemnity?
"A single moon rises over the sea; how many families ascend the tower? Ascending the hall to offer incense: This one portion of incense—
With the utmost reverence, I offer my felicitations for the longevity of the present Emperor, praying for ten thousand, ten thousand, ten thousand times ten thousand years of imperial health.

May Your Majesty’s person remain as undecaying as Heaven and as ever-risen as the midday sun; may you enjoy eternal life and a magnificent reign for ten million years, and may the Great Trichiliocosm universally submit to your righteous rule. Furthermore—
Holding up the incense:

I respectfully offer this for the Governor, the Commander-in-Chief, the Grand Marshal, and the Prefectural Judge, Hua-wen Langzhong, as well as all the civil and military officials of the entire prefecture, that their years of fortune and merit may increase and flourish, and that the True Teaching may be widely disseminated.
Next, holding up the incense: I respectfully offer this for the former abbot of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture.
At Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Monastery, for the sake of repaying the grace of the Dharma-milk, the specially bestowed Chan Master Fuxin, the Great Monk Zeweng, adjusted his robes and took his seat.
He then said: "The eloquent words of the skillful speaker are words that cannot be spoken."
The "trace of the traceless" is that which cannot be traced by any trace. Yesterday, atop a solitary peak, he roared at the moon and slept amidst the clouds;
his joy was boundless. Today, at the crossroads, he drags through mud and water; his fixed karma is difficult to evade.

He laughs at Dongshan, who carried a wooden board to escape fame, and mocks Muzhou, who wove reeds to sell his "sharpness. Yet they fail to realize that whether turning left or right, there is nowhere to go.
This is not possible. How is this known? After the rain, there is a person plowing the green fields; under the bright moon, no dogs bark in the flowering village.
Again, it is recounted that one day Master Zhigong sent someone to deliver a message to Chan Master Dashi of Nanyue:
"Why do you not go down the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings? Why do you instead gaze upward at the clouds and the Milky Way? Dashi replied: "The three periods of time..."
"All Buddhas have been swallowed up by me in a single gulp; where else could there be any sentient beings left to convert? The Master said:
"Zhizang has an inch on his measuring rule, but Sida lacks a star on the end of his scale. Not one of them can escape being measured out. Ultimately, where does the error lie?
Water flowing down the mountain has no intention; a fragment of cloud returning to its cave is fundamentally without mind."
That evening’s informal discourse (xiaochan): The divine light is never obscured; it is a magnificent legacy for all ages. Upon entering this gate, do not harbor intellectual understanding.
When Xinguang first advanced to take charge of the monastery, he resolutely did not wish to establish formal rules;
however, having no other choice, he briefly prepared a communal feast to look after everyone. Yet, alas, there was nothing else to be done. He took up his staff—this very staff!

To see what is right and act with courage; to pull others from poverty and establish them in wealth. To seek even one or half of such a person among the noble—go forth, knowing shame and having a sense of propriety!
*Zhuo!* (A strike of the staff). Abundant in Jiangnan, it is entirely absent in Jiangbei.
Again, he cited the way of Chan Master Fadingeng: "Originally, he intended to remain deeply hidden in mountain caves, living in seclusion until his time had passed.
However, because his late teacher had an unresolved case, he came forth to settle it for him. At that time, a monk stepped forward and asked, "What is this unresolved case?
Dening struck him with his voice as he spoke, saying, "The ancestors have not settled it; the calamity reaches their descendants. Master [Fayan].
It is said: "Oh! A verse formed under the moon and before the wind—someone has already circulated it as a poem by a ghost.
On the occasion of the Spring Retreat, the Master ascended the hall: "One is not; two are not. Where the level marshes end, there are green mountains;
when the yang energy arises, there is no hard ground. This reaches the point where the willows shake the ice and cold eyes are opened wide, and the plum blossoms bear snow.
A smile so full it could be gathered up—this is precisely the non-temporal causal condition; this is called the true offering of the Dharma.
Ultimately, who is the one who knows gratitude? Puhua kicks over the rice table; Linji’s household constantly replenishes the alms bowls.
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: Everywhere it is the Lantern Festival; every household has a bowl of lanterns. The winds of the kalpas cannot extinguish them;
even the Buddha’s hand finds it difficult to illuminate them. I laugh, however, at the old Master Deshan of yore, who lost his eyesight right where the paper candle went out.
"Until now, they have fallen into the dark abyss. Is there anyone who can save them? [The Master] lets out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: One day, Linji and Puhua went together to a donor’s house for a meal.
Linji asked, "A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. Is this the wondrous function of spiritual powers, or is it simply the nature of things as they are?"
Hua kicked over the rice table. Jie (Linji) left. The next day, he went again to a donor’s house for a meal.
Jie asked again, "How does today's offering compare to yesterday's? Hua kicked over the rice table once more. Jie said, "It is so, it is so, but you are far too crude. Hua replied, "Blind fellow!
What 'coarseness' or 'refinement' is there in the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The wind does not come, and the tree does not move."
"Movement! Here is a pair of iron hammers without holes; one of them is the heaviest.
You all, while having no other business beneath your bedding, try weighing them and see."
The Buddha ascended the hall for the occasion of his *nirvāṇa*: "The Tathāgata does not appear in the world, nor is there any *nirvāṇa*.
When spring arrives, the hundred flowers bloom in profusion; when autumn comes, the myriad things wither away. Thus and thus! Pointlessly and pointlessly!
Raise your eyebrows and look closely!"
Ascending the hall: This morning is the fifteenth day of the third month. Peach blossoms fall in profusion like a rain of red.
When Lingyun saw them once and had no doubt, he was merely washing soil with soil. How one can bear this old man Xie Sanlang on his fishing boat;
coming further onto level ground, he drives in stakes and rows the oars. Cold-eyed, Baoen looks at it: a single mu of land, yet three snakes and nine rats.
Ascending the hall: Yesterday was a bustling clamor; today is a profound stillness. Observe the affairs of the bustling within the stillness;
the affairs of the stillness are realized within the bustle—there is nothing to be realized. When spring ends on the Ten Islands, the flowers wither and fall;
the coral forests shine brightly under the blazing sun.
Ascending the hall, he cited the Fifth Patriarch’s address to the assembly: "This summer, the various manors suffered from drought and damage, yet this was not considered a cause for concern.
That one hundred and twenty monks have spent the summer retreat while no one understands the koan of 'The Dog Has No Buddha-nature'—this is truly deeply lamentable.

He continued, "At Bao’en this summer, the various manors were submerged by floods; this is indeed a cause for deep concern. But as for the koan of 'The Dog Has No Buddha-nature,' what [is there to worry about]?"
I have leisure to speak; do you know where to find the place for repaying this kindness? "Throughout my life, I have laid bare my liver and gall toward others;
though we are acquainted, it is as if we were strangers.

This is the small *cán* (private instruction) upon the conclusion of the summer retreat. To raise the Dharma banner and establish the fundamental tenets—clearly, this is the Buddha’s mandate at Caoxi. A cangue upon the neck.
Weighing a thousand catties, they roam the rivers and seas and traverse the mountains and rivers; seeking masters and visiting sages for the sake of Zen meditation.
With mud three feet deep beneath their feet, they let go at the precipice and fall directly into the Iron Ring Mountains. At the top of a hundred-foot pole, what a mess!
How much more so when they sit upon the curved wooden chair, prattling on about this and that, or occupy the long rows of beds, closing their eyes and blinking—this is all nothing but empty space.
Driving in the stake; twisting wood to produce flowers. I have settled your debt of gratitude for you all at once. (He strikes the whisk.
Startled from the evening sky, two or three rows of hawks fly slantwise toward the sea gate.
The monk took his leave of Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "Where there is a Buddha, you must not dwell; there are thorns in the soft mud. Where there is no Buddha, pass by quickly;
to turn your head brings calamity. Even when meeting people three thousand miles away, do not speak of this mistakenly.
As you go out the door, I still repeatedly entrust it to you. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall not go. I do not know who is a true connoisseur."
The Master said: "Plucking the willow blossoms, plucking the willow blossoms; the spring breeze has no fixed course, blowing them up as they pass over to the neighbor's house.

When he went out on his rounds and ascended the hall, he said: "At the single-plank bridge in a village of three households, one bows deeply to repay the price of a greeting; with a smiling face, one accepts a blow from a fist.
How does this compare to the foolish Maitreya in Fenghua County, Mingzhou, who idly pats people on the back when he meets them? Beg me..."
One copper coin.
On the anniversary of Chan Master Foxin’s death, he held up his incense and said: "Tsk! This yellow-faced fellow from Zhejiang—when have I ever known you?
When the precipice collapses, one laughs heartily; though all the people in the great earth try to support him, they cannot. Yet he can be supported. An orange that has crossed the Huai River."
Yet it transforms into a *kī* tree. Entering the hall:
Great fields are shrouded by clouds; the vast sky drips with dew. Everyone has sinews in their eyes;
at every turn, the road is straight ahead. Why is it that when they shift their feet, they stumble past it without realizing? Fine food is not for the hungry to eat.

Upon arriving at the place where the dharma was to be received, the assembly requested him to ascend the seat. An ancient said: "When traveling for the Way, do not return to your hometown; if you return to your hometown, the Way will not be accomplished.
By the stream, an old woman called me by my former name. In the past, those who traveled for the Way near their homes were both bold and cautious.
Guangxiao: In a place where it is difficult for the eyes of the multitude to deceive, one meets the ancients. When traveling on foot, one must return to one's hometown;
upon returning home, do not grow weary of frequenting it. Who would have known that beneath the scholar’s cap lies none other than the person of former sorrows? *Duḥ!*

Ascending the hall, the Master raised this story: When Huangbo was serving as the Head Seat in Nanquan’s assembly, one day he sat in Nanquan’s seat. Just as Nanquan was entering the hall, he asked, "In what year did you begin practicing the Way, Elder? Huangbo replied, "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja. Nanquan said, "You are still but a descendant of Old Wang. Huangbo then moved over to sit in the second seat. The Master offers this verse: The head seat sits in the master’s place; Nanquan asks about the years of his practice. "Before King Bhīṣma," he says— A true son of the old patriarch. He moves to the second seat; The whole assembly is startled. The golden lion roars from within the cave; The jade rabbit leaps out from the moon. The spring breeze stirs the willows; The autumn moon shines on the waters. If you can see through this, You will know that the Buddhas and Patriarchs are all here. If you cannot see through it, You will be lost in the weeds of birth and death. Do you understand? If you do not understand, listen to this: The first seat is empty; the second seat is vacant. The whole world is a single great matter. The bright moon shines upon the clear river; The white clouds float across the blue sky. If you can see this clearly, You will see that the Buddhas and Patriarchs are all here. If you cannot see it clearly, You will be lost in the weeds of birth and death. Do you understand? The peach and plum trees speak not, yet spring fills the courtyard; With songs and drumbeats, we pass the Qingming festival.
Within the pond of some noble villa, A pair of mandarin ducks—how could they ever be painted?
Accepting the invitation from the Twin Pagodas of Pingjiang, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Three years have brought to an end the grudges of the monks;
who would be willing to cast a brick into the void? It is laughable that in my old age I lack the power of stability, yet again I have moved my staff and bowl across the land of Wu."
The Recorded Sayings of the Chan Master of Shouning Wansui Temple at the Twin Pagodas in Pingjiang Prefecture, compiled by Attendants Xingyou and Liaoyuan.

Upon entering the monastery and occupying the abbot’s quarters, he took up the Great Sword (Ta’o) in his hand; having grasped the weight on the scale-head, he acted accordingly. Even a spoon could not lift him.
[The Master] ascends the seat.
Having finished offering incense and making the vow for the Emperor, he takes his place and says: "The sparse rain drips from the four eaves; a single bell rings atop the twin pagodas.

This reveals the true mechanism of the Buddha’s smile upon the Vulture Peak assembly, and discloses the secret instructions of the direct transmission before the peak of Shaoshi. It truly enables the three periods of time..."
The Buddhas knit their brows in the dark; the six generations of patriarchs gaze out from afar with hands pressed to their foreheads.
At New Shouning, one wins nothing but the mouthful of rice to eat. Why? For one sees only the imperial wind forming a single expanse, unaware of where the boundaries lie.
Again, he cited Bao-shou’s opening of the hall: San-sheng brought forward a monk, and Bao-shou struck him.
San-sheng said, "To act for others in such a way not only blinds this monk's eyes, but will blind the people of the entire city of Zhenzhou. Bao-shou then returned to his quarters.
The Master said, "The two elders acting thus was very much like trying to hold water with a stone. If Bao-shou were here today," he said, "I would..."
Someone pushed forward a monk, and [the Master] immediately let out a thunderous shout, making everyone throughout the great earth deaf for three days.
That evening, during the informal discourse (*xiaocan*), before the drum and after the bell, he fully raised a single phrase to break free from the mold and escape the mortar. Here—
Reflect deeply upon this! You have already been buried and lost long ago;

how much more so when you wait for the bells to toll and the drums to beat, for lamps and candles to be arrayed in profusion, and for you to sit and stand with solemnity, engaging in a flurry of questions and answers—what use is that?
Nevertheless, you must further know that there is the scattering of true pearls within a purple silk curtain. (He lets out a shout.)
Again, he raised [the case]: Master Fenyang said, "Even if you manage to enter Fenyang’s gate, you have not yet entered Fenyang’s room.

Even if you enter Fenyang’s room, you have not yet seen Fenyang himself. The Master said, "The Lion of Xihé is indeed fierce and majestic, yet he cannot avoid hiding his body while exposing his shadow.
Shouning is not like this: as soon as one enters Shouning’s gate, one has already entered."
The Chamber of Longevity and Peace. As soon as one enters the Chamber of Longevity and Peace, one immediately beholds the person of Longevity and Peace. Why is this?
Because the wild landscape is no longer interrupted by mountains; the celestial light flows directly through to the waters.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The fences and walls have collapsed; the bridge is broken and the path ends. How much more so now that the year has reached its end?

When one is at the limit, there is penetration; when there is penetration, there is transformation. It is far yet right before one's eyes; it is near yet cannot be seen. He struck his knee and said: "Through the iron wall and silver mountain, a single thread passes."
Master Dachuang of Tianning Monastery in Jiahe ascended the hall for the morning service. He raised the following case:

Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, "Aside from the transmission of the golden robe, what else did the World-Honored One transmit? Kāśyapa called out, "Ānanda! Ānanda responded, "Yes? Kāśyapa said, "Throw down the banner-pole in front of the gate.
The Master offered this verse: Ten thousand acres of wasteland, no one to till it; In a year of famine, the auspicious grain.
The ears of grain grow together; the village elders all know this as an auspicious omen for the nation. For every inch of gold and every inch of earth, one must strive with all one’s might.

Entering the hall [the Master said]: "The fine drizzle of plum rain falls upon the high tiers; in the fifth month, the mountain hermitage is cold as ice. Do not say that heaven and earth have failed their great promise;
it is simply that you have not yet realized that the ground of the mind is scorching heat. Xuedou took a copy of his calligraphy and showed it to people, saying directly: [Text continues]
These dragons and snakes soar and move; the strokes and dots are distinct and clear. Yet, in the midst of "Hūṃ Hūṃ," there is a slight point of ambiguity;
even a drunken Zhang Jian could not distinguish it with certainty.
He ascended the hall and said: "I have come to this land from the beginning, to transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings. One flower opens into five petals; the fruit is borne."
"It is spontaneously accomplished. The Master said, "Master Bodhidharma, for no reason, traded black beans for people's eyes.
You all must take great care!"

When Master Xiyuan went from Mount Jing to Zhongdinghui Temple and ascended the hall for the formal discourse, he said: "The noble guest from the Dragon Abyss possesses a great precious jewel, yet has never easily revealed it.
Today at Shouning, before the assembled multitude, he points it out all at once. This is like a poor man wishing to dwell next to a wealthy one."

Please, Abbot, ascend the hall. The World-Honored One said: "From the Deer Park at the beginning until the Vārāṇasī River at the end, in this interval between the two, I have never uttered a single word.
Suddenly, someone might ask: "From where did you obtain this great treasury of teachings?"
Simply say: "Stop questioning Zeng Xi as if he were Zeng Shen; from of old, a filial son avoids his father’s name.
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall. At the head of the brazier, the talk has neither host nor guest; it cannot be dispersed, nor can it be gathered. Eye meets eye; face looks upon face.
To trigger the mechanism, one must have a crossbow of a thousand *qun*.
When the Monk Dongshan of Kaiyuan in Jianning Prefecture went to Tiger Hill, he ascended the hall and said:

"A person has come from Jian'an and brought a letter from Jingshan, reporting that a single drop from East Creek has surged and burst through the vast ocean, rolling over the Sword Pond until it pervades heaven and earth.
It has caused every fish, dragon, shrimp, and crab to lose its life. Now, how shall we express this single phrase shared by those of the same stream?"
The Way of Birth. In the West, the sun rises in the hour of Mao.

On the day of the Buddha’s birth, he ascended the hall [and said]: "The pure Dharma-body—muddy pigs and scabby dogs; though the Ganges has been washed away, when has it ever been free from defilement?
Yunmen, with his lame leg, performs somersaults with all his might. Shouning takes what he has to settle a deep grievance. Fortunately, there is...
A pair of destitute hands.
Entering the hall in Central China: "The Buddhas of the three periods have not reached the ultimate in their prior practice; the six generations of patriarchs were too far in their final step."
The intermediate phrase: the offense shall not be punished severely. One Buddha, two Dharma, three Saṃgha. Oṃ suru siri svāhā.
Ascending the hall on the Double Yang day:
the frost has settled and the waters have receded; the heavens are high and the air is clear. Wild geese arrive anew, drifting and soaring; the cicadas are silent.
Silent and without sound—this is the age-old custom of ascending heights to perceive the true nature of heaven, earth, and the myriad things.
I shall briefly use a touch of worldly flavor to change the eyes of all of you. (He plants his staff. Do not mistake the markings on the scale.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised up the staff and said, citing Chan Master Yunfeng Yue: "If you recognize the master’s staff, the business of a lifetime of study is finished.
He then held it up and asked, "Which of these is the master’s staff? Which is the business of study?

He then laid the staff across his shoulder and said, "Carrying the knotted staff slung over my shoulder, I look not back at men; I go straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. The Master said, "Do not blame me for sitting here so often."
Exhortation to Partake: Since our parting, I have rarely seen you.
Setting out for Qingliang in Jiankang Prefecture, I bid farewell to the assembly from the high seat. A mere trifle of lingering goods;

nine years of sitting in cold silence—yet people immediately begin to deliberate on its worth, failing to realize they have once again missed the mark. By the walls of Shitou City, there are naturally those who understand; the tall bamboos stand alone.
Rain brings light knocks upon the jade; yellow chrysanthemums welcome autumn with half-revealed gold.
Compiled by the attendants Shan-zhi and Jing-zheng for the *Record of Sayings* of Qingliang Guanghui Chan Temple in Jiankang Prefecture.

Entering the hall. After offering incense to pray for the Emperor, he takes his seat and says: "The Way has no form; those who gaze upon it cannot perceive it. Before the crags, flakes of flower-rain fly."
The Way has no fixed direction; practitioners are unable to reach it. On the road, there is but a single signpost for five *li*.

Yet, if one perceives and arrives at it directly and intimately, what hindrance is there to coming or going? By the side of the Gusu Terrace, clouds rush and lightning rolls; by the edge of Shitou City, grasses bow and winds sweep.
The gate leading upward is flung wide open, and the Eye of the True Dharma is extinguished. How limitless is the pure breeze beyond the threshold!
Again, it is related that Asanga visited Mañjuśrī. Mañjuśrī asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained in the south?

Asanga replied, "In the age of the final dharma, the bhikṣus observe the precepts and discipline only sparingly. Mañjuśrī asked, "How large is the assembly? Asanga replied, "It consists of either three hundred or five hundred."

Zhao asked Mañjuśrī, "How do you maintain the community here? Mañjuśrī replied, "Ordinary people and sages dwell together; dragons and snakes are intermingled. Zhao asked, "How many followers are there?

Mañjuśrī said, "Three before, three after, three times three. The Master [Yunmen] said, "Throughout antiquity and today, those who have deliberated on this have all fallen into the trap of numerical calculation.
When someone asked Qingliang how he maintained the community, he simply said, "When the water arrives, the channel is formed."
That evening’s informal discourse: The boundless realms of all lands are not separated from one another by so much as a hair’s tip. Mountains encircle the ancient capital, which remains whole;
Ten thousand ages of past and present never depart from this very moment of thought. Tides strike the empty city and return in silence.
Thus, one immediately perceives the mutual fusion of guest and host, where wind and clouds move as one.

Yet, as for the ten thousand bodhisattvas within Mount Qingliang, they cannot be found anywhere—where, then, does the fault lie? He strikes the whisk. "The heavens are high; who lends an ear? The earth is vast;
few are those who understand."
Again, Fayan raised up his dharma-eye and showed it to the assembly, saying: "If you recognize this bench, there is more than enough room around it.
Yunmen said: "If you recognize this bench, heaven and earth are vastly different. Qingliang said: "If you recognize this bench, it is precisely the right time to put on your robes and eat your meal."
Master Quan Guanbo ascended the hall and said: "Clearing the fields to plant millet—eating by day and sleeping by night—Miaoxi and Nanquan, father and son, certainly did not waste their time;

yet they still fell into the trap of worldly effort. This mountain monk this summer has been eating 'refreshing' rice, running north and rushing south, borrowing the Phoenix Terrace to speak of east and west.
Will I thus escape the ridicule and laughter of onlookers? [He raises his whisk.]”
The Master said: "Once power is in one's hand, watch when the command is put into effect.

[On the occasion of] ascending the hall to pray for rain, he cited Yunmen’s words: "Now that the summer solstice has passed," and [Yunmen] struck the meditation seat, saying, "Bring forth a phrase for this point!
He himself provided the substitute response: "Tāmri. He also said: "Tāmrijñāna. And again: "Kha. The Master remarked: "Yun..."

The "Gate" is the mantra of the Single Path; do not let it become turbid or cool. Now that the summer retreat is concluded, at the point where there is no striking or clashing, one must strictly avoid speaking of it.
*Cili cili*, all outflows, all outflows. "Coolness" is the mantra of the Single Path.
Nor can one deceive others. Why? One merely sees a fragment of cloud arise in the azure sky, yet one does not know that the intent of the rain lies upon another mountain.
Entering the hall [he said]: "If you have been here, go drink tea; if you have not been here, go drink tea. Zhaozhou has laid bare his very liver and gall—how much!
Lacking a sense of shame or remorse, you wear horns and shed fur, wandering among the ranks of other species.

At the winter solstice, during this small-scale *sīmān* (private instruction), before the withered tree at the crag’s edge, many diverging paths lie ahead; beneath the bottom of the vast ocean, how many times has the mulberry field been transformed?
This mountain monk cannot help but point out a level and direct path for all of you to tread upon—a place prior to the differentiation of heaven and earth, where yin and yang have not yet reached.
[He draws a stroke with his whisk. The fissure in the ice is split open;
the warmth from beneath one's feet breaks through. A glimpse of wind and clouds reveals the seasonal conditions before one’s eyes. Finished.
What season is it after all? Winter is acting as if it were spring.
[The Master] ascends the hall and cites the story of Linji asking Huangbo about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma. The Master offers this verse:
"Before Mount Huangbo, he brought his uncut jade; Only at Ga'ang Beach did he first realize his shame. Though he sought the price of a 'linked city,' Until now..."
Now the pain has not yet ceased.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "If one discusses this matter, it cannot be described and cannot be named. 'The eyes do not look elsewhere'—it is like a cat watching a mouse hole;
there is no place to set down the mouth. 'The dog licks the hot oil cauldron'—even if you were deaf from hearing the striking of the bamboo, or saw the peach blossoms..."
And yet he was blind. On this very day at noon, he struck the third watch.
Compiled by the attendants Facong, Shaoxun, and Puzhang for the *Record of the Zen Teachings* of the Wannian Baoen Guangxiao Chan Temple in Taizhou.
Occupying the square measure of the abbot’s quarters, he drives in the stakes and rows the oars;

unmooring the lines and setting the boat adrift, even if he could barefootly play with the bright moon and tread upon the sky beneath the waves of the Five Lakes—*he lets out a shout*. For now, step aside.

Having ascended the seat, offered incense, and completed the prayers for the Emperor, he took his place and said: "In deep mountains and rocky cliffs, there are ancient teachings of the Buddha; in level fields and shallow grasses,"
He releases the "burnt-tailed tiger," which immediately causes wind to rise through ten thousand ravines and clouds to surge from a thousand peaks.
Mount Huading, forty-eight thousand *zhang* high, is cast downwind; the five hundred and sixteen ranks of Arhats have no place to hide.

There is nothing left to be witnessed by the eye, so how could it involve verbal explanation? One may thus realize that person and environment are one suchness, and fuse past and present within this very thought. This can be...
To maintain the incense offerings at Guling is to repay the extraordinary grace of the successive sagely emperors. What serves as proof?
He raises his whisk and says: "Half-melted snow by the Huashi Bridge; a single point of spring within the Penglai Caves."
Again, he cited the way of National Teacher Shao: "At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of this world; outside of mind there is no dharma—every eye meets the green mountains.
The Master said: "National Teacher Shao went from long poverty to sudden wealth, yet he claimed that even the beauty of the whole city could not exchange for it.
Looking at it as level fields, it is still like casting away gold to embrace common bricks."

That evening’s informal discourse: To the north of Tiantai’s North Stone Bridge, there is a single phrase that the Old Man with the Yellow Face could not clarify throughout his three hundred and sixty-odd assemblies.
The Old Barbarian with the Missing Teeth came ten thousand *li* from the West and said nothing but “I do not know.
It was as chilling as driving six horses with a rotten rope; it was as precarious as pulling a thousand *jin* with a single hair. New Growth.
Old man! Without cause, he let his mouth slip and spoke out, acting as a "joyous son" for entering the gate.
(He lets out a shout. Entering the hall: The Eight Peaks rise steeply; the twin streams flow murmuring. Moment by moment, face to face; day after day, it is proclaimed.
Pity the pierced-eared guests who wrongly blame Old Pingtian.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring mountains are drenched in deep azure; the spring grasses stretch across the sky in emerald green. The water buffalo within the pen greedily craves the lushness, and the cowherd boy exhausts all the strength of his life in tending it.
With his whisk, he made the gesture of whipping a bull and cried out, "Chit! Chit!"

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The mind of the Great Immortal of the land of Zhuyue has been secretly transmitted from east to west. I inform you all, you practitioners of Chan: you must realize it for yourselves through and through.
To realize it is not non-existent; but what exactly was secretly transmitted? A flash of lightning follows the thunder of the following night;
the sound of rain on the eaves continues from the previous ten days."
Master Guangrun ascends the hall: "The source of Dongjian’s stream flows with a clear, resonant sound;

it moistens the great thousandfold world, yet not a single drop of gold remains. [He raises his staff and strikes once. The flying waterfall at Stone Bridge plunges a thousand fathoms—it does not flow from this place."
On the anniversary of Emperor Huizong’s death, he ascended the hall and said: "How distant is the Way? It is true in every encounter. A single hair swallows the vast ocean.
How distant is the Sage? To embody it is to become divine. At the tips of a hundred grasses is the Dharma-body;
there is no distinction between the barbarian and the Chinese, nor any gap between life and death. Do you know the phrase for repaying kindness? He struck the whisk. Eight.
The waters of the twin gullies flow at the peaks; a single thought is the fragrance of ten thousand years.
When the Buddha ascended the path, the Old Barbarian carried a single shoulder-load of non-awakening. For six years he deliberated, yet could not cast it away;
only when he opened his eyes before Mount Zhengjue did he realize he had once again mistaken the markings on the scale for the true weight.
In the eighth year of Chunyou, celestial envoys entered the mountain.
Respectfully receiving the imperial decree, they prepared offerings for the Arhats and ordained monastic members. Ascending the seat, they offered incense and prayed for the Emperor, vowing:
"May that which is neither smoke nor mist pervade the Dharma-realm boundlessly; may it serve as an auspicious omen and a blessing, praying for the prosperity of the state and its people."
This is a source of great celebration. A monk came forward and asked: "The Sage’s grace is vast and great; descending upon Tiantai, he brushes through the mists and clouds as two paths open.
Amidst the clouds over Fangguang, the golden chime resounds; the Venerable Banzhou smiles, his cheeks full.

The student stepped forward and requested, "Please, Master, proclaim the teaching. He replied, "By the heavens, there is much rain and dew; even withered wood knows how to bloom. The student pressed further, "A single phrase—"

Transcending far beyond past and present, for ten thousand years I reverently pray for the Sage and Enlightened Sovereign. The Emperor replied: "Throughout the four seas, songs of praise resound as the sun and moon shine bright.
The Master advanced and said: "I recall King Aśoka asking Piṇḍola: 'I have heard that you, Venerable One, have personally seen the Buddha;
is this so? The Venerable One raised his eyebrows with his hand and asked: 'Do you understand? The King said: 'I do not understand. At that time, it was like this..."

"What? he asked. The answer was, "Like lacquer poured into glue. The questioner pressed further, "When the Naga King of Lake Anavatapta invited the Buddha for a meal, you were also included among their number;
what then? The answer was, "There is grit in the rice. The questioner pressed further, "Right now, the five hundred Arhats are all present at this assembly;
ultimately, what kind of resonance or transformation has occurred? The answer was, "The alms bowl is held aloft with incense."
Ji Guo said: "The cinnabar tree hangs over ten thousand-year pines. Jin said: "In the Great Peace there are signs, yet originally there are no signs;
ordinary people, sages, and all sentient beings are one family. The Master replied: "The nest knows the wind; the burrow knows the rain. Jin said:

"Do you permit this student to offer a benediction? The Master replied: "Even within a rat’s mouth there are tusks of ivory. Jin said: "Huading Peak is eighteen thousand feet high. The Master replied: "Long."

"To create a Mount Longevity for Your Majesty. He replied, "Only by knowing gratitude can one understand how to repay it. The monk bowed. Thereupon [the Master] said: "The Great Dharma has no exterior;
it triggers the mechanism of Heaven and Earth revealed in their nakedness. The ultimate mirror is impartial; it reaches the furthest limits of the sun and moon’s illumination.
Seated at the summit of Vairocana, he manifests within the realm of Jambudvīpa. Responding to reality without dependence, he sports in liberation."

Through supernormal powers, at times the jewel-torches divide their radiance, making the *tāmarasa* flowers blossom brilliantly by the bridge; at other times the golden bells fall with a resonant peal, manifesting the Vaipulya teachings amidst the deep clouds.
Never abandoning the Tathāgata’s gate of transformative deliverance, they bring to fruition the ocean of sentient beings’ practices and vows.
As for this phrase that is utterly selfless—how shall it be struck forth? With a single sweep of the whisk, the pine branch sweeps clean the gray moss from the stone;
sitting, one watches the clouds return from beyond the heavens.
The Abbot ascends the hall for the supervision of the harvest: "A single leaf falls, and autumn comes to all under heaven. White clouds and flowing waters drift together in leisurely ease.
A single rain moistens the great earth; from high and low, the grain fields are filled to the brim. Is there anyone who does not recognize the Emperor’s power?
As the setting sun slants its light, one plays the flute while riding backward upon an ox."
Incense Offering for the Anniversary of Chan Master Fuxin The waters of East Lake and West Lake surge with waves that strike the heavens;
Mount Yujing and Mount Roudou wind and turn a hundred times, then a thousand more. On the level fields, though there be the five rebellious acts, there is no hidden pit.
Displaying the family style, he inserts the incense and says: "The iron cauldron and the tea kettle are not the same."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The white clouds are limpid; the yellow leaves rustle. This frugal livelihood of poverty does not reside in the staff.

Ascending the hall, he said: "In these advanced years, I am incapable of a hundred things. He took up his staff and said, "Leaning on a solitary cane amidst the shadows of ancient pines," and struck once.

Ascending the hall: Yang declines and Yin wanes; the pines wither and the rocks grow gaunt. By the stream, the willows still knit their brows;

A letter from Master Wujing of Yangshan arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "In sixty years of time, east surges and west sinks;

Shifting the Southern Dipper and turning the Northern Dipper, he fashions a single vessel of heaven and earth.
Swallowing the thorny plum and piercing through the golden ring—this is but the everyday meal. Moving freely and spontaneously, responding appropriately at every moment, like a fish drinking water.
Cold and warmth are known by oneself; like a shadow following a form, long and short are both seen. When the bells and drums do not sound, what can be said of ritual and music?
Questions and answers fly back and forth, yet neither person nor environment is deprived. Although this is so, it is still only half-raised.
As for that one phrase of the "full raising," how can it be proclaimed? He strikes the whisk: "The winter solstice and the Cold Food Festival—one hundred and five days apart."

[The Master] said, "It mostly rests upon ten-thousand-year branches.

[The Master] said: "The people's homes for a thousand li plow through rain and dew; beyond the clouds in the Nine Heavens, they build sand embankments. The attendant asked:

"What auspicious omens have the honored officials of the entire prefecture? He replied: "The sun and moon open the Imperial Way; those in official robes prostrate before the Purple Palace. The monk bowed in reverence.

He then said: "The One True Reality is unmoving, encompassing all divisions within the Dharma-realm; the myriad transformations secretly penetrate, opening up the domain of longevity across the eight wildernesses.
Heaven and earth are settled in great peace; sun and moon move in their courses. Possessing ten thousand virtues, it is called the Most Honored One; it appears for the sake of the One Great Matter.
It truly causes rainbows to flow and lightning to swirl, mountains to stand firm and peaks to cry out. To what does he point as proof? He struck his whisk.
My son, a vermilion phoenix comes from atop the branches of the azure *wú* tree; purple *zhī* fungi grow before the withered trees on the crag.
West Rock Master of Nengren at Yanshan ascends the hall: At the peak of Shuangjing, within the city of Gusu—when you scold me, I spare you for your sharp beak;
when you spit at me, I spare you for your splashing water. Dreaming, we may share a bed; upon waking, it was originally not so.
It is so: eighteen thousand *zhang* reach the azure heavens; forty-nine tiers rise up through the clouds.
Not separated by even a hair’s breadth for three hundred *li*, the echoes of the evil sounds of those coming and going have not yet ceased.
Venerable Ānanda ascends the hall: Before the tower of Beigù, the field of vision is vast; The snowy waves of the Long River splash with a chilling cold.
Now, as we hold hands and gaze upon Mount Huāzhǐng, How does this compare to leaning together on the railing in years past?
The Buddha ascends the hall on his birthday. Before he had even emerged from his mother’s womb, he was already a bit too much; looking around in the four directions, he could not lift his foot.

From that moment on, he began to tell great lies, bringing calamity upon the men and women of many households. Although more than two thousand years have passed, this still causes people to harbor resentment to the very marrow of their bones.
How can one speak of such an enemy? [He] raises his whisk: "The handle of the ladle is in my hand."
Entering the city, I return to the hall. The fields’ silkworms and wheat are ripe; On the mountain paths, the green shade is fresh.
The cuckoo cries until its blood is spent— Do you know for whose sake? Let not this spring of one year be wasted.
Lecturer Sheng of Daci Shiting ascended the hall. Dingguang beckoned with his hand; the stubborn rock nodded its head.

Without opening his mouth, the Great Meaning was already complete. Is this the meaning of the Patriarchs? Or the meaning of the Teachings? This entire assembly remains as solemn as if it had never dispersed.
Together we ride the bright moon across the vast ocean.

A Small Session for the Summer Retreat: The Way has no fixed location; realization is beyond all rungs of a ladder. It does not abide in the pure field of awakening, nor does it swim within the great ocean of nirvana.
Streams, mountains, clouds, and moon—everywhere they are the same; Spring, summer, autumn, and winter—year after year they are alike.
Sword suspended between the brows, talisman hung behind the elbow—what more need be said of dwelling in peace within body and mind, or the wisdom of equanimity?
He raises his whisk: Great renunciation clouds enshroud the mountain peaks; thunder from the stone bridge sprays forth, as cold as snow and frost.
Ascending the hall at the beginning of the summer retreat: the assembly from the ten directions—bricks, tiles, and clods of earth—remain unmoved by even a hair’s breadth.
He plants his staff, and in a single stroke, everything is shattered to pieces. Every single pearl of the black dragon shines upon the vast blue sea.
The Emperor Huizong’s Memorial Day: Entering the Hall. The springtime has passed once more for another year; Fragrant breezes vainly lock in the mists of Shanglin Park.
If you wish to know the true place of eternal joy and wandering, It lies by the Fangguang Bridge, where no cuckoos cry.
Ascending the hall on the Dragon Boat Festival: All the world is drunk, yet I alone am sober; the entire age is turbid, yet I alone am pure.
Qu Yuan of the Three Clans—how he played the zither before the Nymph of the Xiang! The cloud-chariots glide through the mist; the mountain ghosts dwell in the profound darkness.
"If one does not brandish the sword, the fisherman will take refuge in his nest. He raises his staff and strikes once, saying: "When the music ends, the people are gone;
on the river, several peaks stand green."
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the National Foundation Day: On Mount Shou at Tiantai, there are forty-eight thousand *zhang*.

As the sun rises over the vast blue sea, its light first strikes the mountain peak. There, the jade-like trees blossom in radiant splendor, while the scarlet ratcheted staff stands out against the gnarled bark. The *āryas* sound their golden gongs.
Prince Jin’s jade flute resounds; leaning against pines, he points to the kalpa-stone. Controlling cranes, he watches the ocean swell. Together we celebrate ten million years;
our Sovereign’s longevity is immeasurable.

Ascending the hall, he raised the case of the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū: "For ten kalpas he sat at the site of enlightenment; yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him, and he could not attain the Way of the Buddha.

When both [subject and object] are extinguished, one sees that the single assembly on Vulture Peak remains solemnly as if it had never dispersed. One speaks without speaking; one transmits without transmitting.
Striking the whisk: a single melody of Great Peace to celebrate the longevity of Yao.
Furthermore, it is recounted that Emperor Xiaozong asked the former abbot of this mountain, Chan Master Fozhao:
"When Śākyamuni Buddha entered the mountains for six years, what did he accomplish? Fozhao replied: "I thought—"
Your Majesty has forgotten; I, this monk, have a verse: The question was extraordinary, the answer intimate; A single phrase in the presence of the sun settles all under heaven.
The Snowy Mountains shine high against the Golden Hall; Ten-thousand-year reign, majestic and towering, serves the Most Honored One.

Ascending the hall on the occasion of the National Foundation Day: His intelligence surpasses all his peers; his dignified bearing rectifies the world. Crossing oceans and climbing mountains, all have returned to this supreme transformation.
How can one perceive this? Within the shadows of the crags and ferns, he strides like an auspicious qilin; at the head of the verdant meadows, he neighs like a spirited steed.
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: "Ciming placed a basin of water, a single sword, and a pair of straw sandals in his room.
Whenever a monk arrived, he would point them out to him. The Master said: 'Those who have already passed through the barrier walk away with their sleeves flapping;
those who see the shadow of the whip are not fine horses.'"
Record of the Sayings of Jingshan Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Temple, compiled by Attendant Huiyun Ruozhou. At the Mountain Gate:
The five peaks of the Double Path (Shuangjing) stand wide open; yet one cannot plant one’s feet within them. Dragons soar and phoenixes dance.
The Imperial Edict: The vermilion phoenix dances in the nine heavens; a single phrase is sealed with purple clay. Truly, it transforms without words and accords without appointment.
The wind follows the tiger, and the clouds follow the dragon.
The Dharma Seat: When waters run dry and clouds have vanished, one reaches the heights of the sky; yet upon one's head, the falling snow has not yet melted.
An aged gait should only suit level ground; I know not for what reason I have once again ascended this height.
Ascending the seat, he offered incense, saying:

"This single offering of incense is respectfully presented to pray for the longevity of the current Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years! May Your Majesty’s imperial destiny be auspiciously inaugurated, establishing a great enterprise in the year of Gengshen;
may the vast foundation of ten thousand generations endure through the cycles of the Jiazi year."
This incense is respectfully offered to Her Majesty the Empress.
Ten thousand blessings, ten thousand blessings! We humbly pray that the *jiū* birds may sing in harmony, hearing the true sounds of a well-governed age;
and that the azure-feathered birds may fly and cry out, conveying the tidings of the Immortals’ realm.

This incense is offered for the sake of His Imperial Highness the Crown Prince. We humbly pray that, in presiding over the military and overseeing the state, he may understand the fundamental source of governance and transformation;
and in reverently transmitting the teachings of his honored masters, he may rectify the Great Way of cultivating the Path.
This incense is offered in honor of the Grand Tutor, Palace Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, and Duke of the State.

May the civil and military officials of the Five Ministries and the entire court likewise increase their years of longevity and receive greater emolument. We humbly pray that your singular virtue may match the heavens, bringing forth clarity and brilliance.
Regarding Your Majesty’s service under Yao and Shun, you have held the rank of the Three Dukes and achieved great merit like that of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou.

This incense is offered for the sake of the Vice Minister, the Governor, as well as the civil and military officials. We humbly pray that you may carry forth the current and proclaim the transformation, becoming the most eminent among the Nine Provinces.
First, in managing the difficult and resolving the complex, you surpassed the ranks of the Three Kings.
This incense is respectfully offered for the sake of the Former Abbot, the current thirty-second patriarch of this mountain, the specially bestowed Zen Master Fuxin, Dahu Zeweng.
Furthermore, in order to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk, he took his seat and said:
"The Dharma is not hidden; the Way has no front or back. [I shall now] drive out the stones, large and small, from the deep mountains and rocky cliffs."
Examine whether or not there is a face within the bustling marketplace of the red dust.

Only when the bright moon and clear wind allow for freedom in both revealing and concealing will the trees, forests, water, and birds preach the Dharma endlessly. Since time immemorial, Xinjingshan’s mouth has been narrow;

he has only accepted what is already accomplished and enjoyed the light of a peaceful era. On what basis does he do so? From atop the Hanying Pavilion, he gazes toward the Eastern Sea, soaring toward the clouds.
"From the peak, I bow to Nanyue.
He spoke again: "Mazu sent Zhizang to deliver a letter to National Teacher Yi of Shangguo. Upon opening it, Yi saw a perfect circle (a *yuanxiang*) within;
he placed a single dot inside it and returned the seal. When National Teacher Zhong heard of this, he said, 'Qinshan was still deluded by Master Ma.'"
The Master’s verse says: To present face-to-face is still not enough; How could it convey greetings written on paper?
Pity those who, though sharing the same breeze from a thousand miles away, Stiffly regard the outer envelope as the message itself.
This evening’s formal inquiry: When Mahākāśyapa sealed his room at Mount Magadha, there was a carp in the mountain stream;

when Vimalakīrti remained silent at Vaiśālī, there was dust and weeds at the bottom of the well. This family inheritance, which could not have been fully exhausted even after two thousand years of preaching, has tonight been brought forth all at once by Jingshan.
Do you all know it? (He strikes a circular mark with his whisk. No need for further effort.
A stone mirror is suspended; at dawn, the roosters crow of themselves.
Jueyuan (White Cloud) showed the assembly, saying: "Again and again I call for you, yet you do not return home; You greedily go out the gate to play with dust and sand.
Every year, in the third month, Throughout the city, peonies bloom everywhere. If you do not know how to be a guest...
I trouble you, Master. Jing Mountain also has a verse: "Without needing to be called, one returns home of one's own accord;
what need is there to add more sand to the eyes? If one is a true scion of my house, they will pluck the willow blossoms three thousand miles away."
Incense Offering for the Memorial of Chan Master Fuxin: In those days, I truly knew nothing of the seasons; I once stood here before the courtyard in deep snow.
There was not a single dharma that could stir my emotions; my heart, once embroidered with silk, had turned to iron. My grievances cannot be washed away and my resentment is hard to erase;
I burn this single incense stick—a blend of donkey urine and sandalwood.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Layman Lu Xuan asked Nanquan, “Master Zhao is truly extraordinary;

he understands that ‘Heaven and earth share the same root with me, and all things are one body with me. Nanquan pointed to a flower in the courtyard and said, “Layman, do you acknowledge this? The Layman responded, “Yes.

Nanquan said, “When people of this age see this single stalk of a flower, it is as if they were dreaming. The Master then offered this verse: “The myriad trees are frozen, [The myriad flowers are withered.]”
Intending to break it, the solitary root turns warm on its own. Deep within the snows of the village ahead, a single branch has blossomed last night.
Ascending the Dharma Hall on New Year’s Day: Last year, ascending the mountain on the first day of the first month, all matters were in a state of chaos.

This year, ascending the hall on the first day of the first month, all things are fully completed. Let the succession of years pass as they may and let time and light change; I now take up the master’s staff.
The staff. There is only the master’s staff, still as black as lacquer. *Thwack!* The rest of the text is long;
it is entrusted for another day.
(Buddhas and Patriarchs’ Verses of Praise)
The manifestation of leaving the mountains:
before the mountain of perfect enlightenment, he broke his original vow. Though he clearly possesses a mouth, it is difficult even to open.
Who would have known that before entering Māyā’s womb, he had already given rise to the seeds of calamity in Jambudvīpa?
The deaf-mute Guanyin enters meditative absorption within the water-moon light; with eyes wide open, he clearly perceives all sensory objects.
Do not say that his skillful means go unrecognized; the deaf-mute speaks from beginning to end to others.
The lotus leaf motif—a single petal of the lotus, a boat upon the sea of suffering. Wherever you may drift with the current, simply drift with it;
holding the one-hundred-and-eight beads in hand, you should count them from the beginning without ceasing, day and night.
Dharma crossed the river, treading upon the earth’s axis and overturning the celestial pivot. The entire nation pursued him, yet he did not return. His path departed with a body as light as a leaf;
the Changjiang’s waves remain like mountains through the ages.
The boat drifts slowly and languidly across waves of mist and smoke; I strike the oars and sing long songs and short ones.
Had I not encountered the scaled dragon that swallows the straight hook, what would I have done with this moonlit boat full to the brim?
Hanshan drags his clogs while holding a broom;

beneath his feet are broken wooden sandals, and in his hand he carries a fresh rattan brush. Unable to put them down, he drags them along as he goes, smiling and pointing at those of this age who do not realize they exist.
Picking up a vegetable basket and a string of dried eggplants, he holds the string of dried eggplants in his hand.
The basket contains the dregs of bitter herbs; as he carelessly drags it along meeting people, one wonders whose palate these flavors will fall upon.
The Venerable Master Zhe swallowed the lethal poison of Mount Mao; he employed the "transcendental errors" of Linji. In six places he sold dogs while hanging up sheep;
throughout the four seas he overturned the pools and toppled the mountains. Error! Error! Fortunately, no one followed his example.

Receiving instruction from my master, I observed the head monk weaving a fence to protect the bamboo, leading water to irrigate the flowers, the fine breeze among the pines, and the leaning staff upon the rocks. My true face is clearly manifest right now;
who among his descendants will maintain this way of life? Through kalpas, it has caused people inexhaustible regret, precisely because he taught me to "put on" [the robes].
Kāṣāya. [This concludes] the Verses on Parting from Death by Xinxin.
The Gāthā of the Sixth Patriarch: "The Sixth Patriarch was no hero of those days; Carrying firewood, his shoulder-pole broke, and he was quite coarse. Yet at the assembly at Huangmei, Bodhi..."
A tree: one axe-stroke cuts it down at the root until nothing remains.
He hires someone to write on the wall while he himself applies plaster. "White ground is white; black ground is black. How many seekers of the sword has he deceived!
Vast and empty, they merely copy the gourd from the model.
Clearly there is a verse stating that "there is no thing," yet in the end, it emerges from the prisoner's own mouth. Like a sacred tortoise dragging its tail, how pitiable!
It is much like clutching one's stolen goods while crying out for injustice.
Yet he accepted another’s single alms-bowl; when pursued by others, he wasted his breath in excuses.
Such a reckless and idle fellow—thankfully, his descendants have no need for him.
The Chancellor summoned me with his decree;
amidst the piles of ice and snow, ten thousand trees were crushed. Warmth was blown from the side of the sun to reach the river plum. The withered branch sighed to itself:
"Born in the north, even if I obtain the spring breeze, I shall not bloom."
North Hall sends cloth for my son;
this year marks the beginning of our poverty. Having sold the single bolt of cloth, I am left with nothing but my own person. My wife’s heart is filled with anxious concern as she sends it again;
wrapped up and brought here, it feels all the more alien.

I bid farewell to Old Gao, whose auspicious presence makes all quarters a theater of laughter. Look, look! Upon the stage, it is you who are now in a hurry. Fine wine has never been hidden in deep alleys;
do not resent the spring breeze for making the dancing sleeves so long.
Chan Master Wuan Mengjie served a meal to the monks in his hermitage:
"A single thing is fundamentally non-existent; it is used to feed blind donkeys throughout all quarters. He tested those who could not recognize their shame:
"Junshan swallowed Lake Dongting."
Farewell, Vice Minister Dong:
Halting at the hillside or flowing along, there is no fixed form. The Jade Unicorn has issued its command to reach this forest gate. The frozen clouds do not rise with the spring breeze;
I have truly failed to enjoy half the green of Mount Zhong.
I present this to the physiognomist:
Thick mists and rising clouds cannot be parted; The ancient pines and strange rocks stand tall and majestic. Within this, it is easy to see yet difficult to perceive;
It takes another visit from you, Master, to discern it once more.
Sent by Zen practitioner Sōshin (at that time, Dai-sensei Ōkawa Masasuke, acting on the command of Jōji):
The noble custom of roasting yams belongs to your father; He closed his door and knew not the purple imperial seal. May you, my son, convey my profound sentiments;
I fear we shall meet again beneath the moon at the third watch.
Seeing off Chan Master Chao (the junior disciple Bielu):
The parting song at Yunfeng has long been mournful; In lamentation, there is no one to continue the broken strings. A vast, pure sound fills the Teao and She rivers;
Under the bright moon, there are still boats returning at night.
I send this traveling seat-cushion and straw hat to He Yunzheng, as the evening sun sets atop Mount Ding. Steep cliffs and perilous steps wind like sheep’s intestines;
Having probed ahead for the depth of the stream, He must surely laugh at the long handle of my ladle on the level fields.
The Venerable of Bian Mountain at Tiandong invites me:
"How many brothers are there now throughout the four seas? Flying crosswise and soaring straight upward, you shake the glory of our clan.
I am idly reclining while you are beset by illness; how can this intention be fully expressed?"
A Petition to Director of Transport Wu of Jingxi, Requesting the Myriad-Year-Old Pine to the South of Stone Bridge:
For six years, I have personally sealed its pure shade; With a single clap of thunder, it was startled into transformation.
It shall once again be moved upward to Mount Zhurong’s Peak.
The Zen practitioner Songfu:
leaves in the forest, about to fall but not yet fallen; clouds at the edge of heaven, flying south and north.
If you can realize the meaning of leaving home upon returning home, the autumn is tenfold at the ferry crossing of Yangzi.

From the beginning, when the myriad phenomena reach their ultimate limit, one's own body is revealed alone. From birth until old age, there is no distance between oneself and others. Putting on clothes and eating food are ordinary matters;
why has this ever-been-present truth been sought from another?
Presented to Xu Duliang:
Your subtle craftsmanship is peerless; you wield the wind-blown axe without relying on the square or the compass.
On the day you achieve success under the gate of Nanshan, you will put to shame all those who labor with bloodied fingers.
Presenting Tang-dynasty brushes to the Arhat for the Chancellor Jia:
Holding a *palm-leaf* scripture while seated upon a *piṇḍa* rock, he remains silent, for words are too many. All marks are utterly empty, yet he still employs them to dispel [delusion].
In the city of Vaiśālī, he questioned Vimalakīrti.
Harmony. An Imperial Ode on the Thousand Buddhas of Lingyin:
Only the Buddha and the Buddha are equal and without distinction. Their measure is comparable to the great void; their countenances are like the full moon. The true form is unborn.
Deluded views have their cessation; a single thought-moment is ten thousand years. Like snow falling upon a red-hot furnace—this is the transmission from Jiangxi to Fuzang.
Alas, how vast and remote is this Way! One flower blooms in five petals, yet they open and then fall; the branches and the offshoots divide and do not cease.
Divided. Now and then, past and present, all have fallen into confusion. There was an ancestor who emerged from the Western Hills;

during the Chunxi era, he once performed great deeds. Upon the Golden Hall, the sun and moon shone bright; his straw sandals repeatedly hung from the corner of the Dragon Bed. Even now, his descendants fill the Great Tang.
They have eclipsed the family tradition, their reputation having turned foul. To restore the son is indeed the neighbor from the West; towering alone, he stands forth.

Standing like a crane amidst a flock of chickens, he returns to Confucianism and Daoism, cleansing them with painful thoroughness. To look up to former sages without shame, one must realize that level fields and perilous heights offer no place for lodging.
For three years he sat in cold seclusion, sharing in such desolation. Laughing, he points to the golden scriptures bound upon high shelves;
across the ten-thousand-li autumn sky, his wings cannot be tethered. Parting at the crossroads, he bids me farewell and hopes for a single word: "On the Way—do not, do not, do not, do not, do not!"
Seeing off Master Yuàn as he travels through Jianghuai—three days today, four tomorrow.
We compose verses together like a troupe of monkeys playing; seven stars of the Southern Dipper, eight stars of the Northern Dipper.
The entire Great Canon of Teachings—*alala*! Master Yuàn, you shall not linger long in this land of moisture; the spring breeze shall revitalize the tip of your staff.
The Hu monk does not know where Old Xiao dwells; for a thousand ages, the long river flows on without ceasing.
The weeds of ignorance bury the reeds, and the mournful wind whistles as the Hu-pipa flies. When asked to provide words for a funeral procession, they fill the void of space and cannot be uttered.
Only when mountains and seas are overturned and one meets a true知音 (zhiyin) do common shards and rubble become pure gold.
He saw off Chan Attendant Chè of Huqiu to Lingyin (the latter being the son of Jíshí).
The Head Seat explained the matter for the sake of the assembly.
When Wén Héshàng of Yú’ān received the Imperial decree to serve as abbot of Zífú Chán Temple, he accepted the invitation at that very temple.

The Master leads the assembly. At the side of Linglong Rock, there is no contriving; a single pressure causes the whole body to fall over the precipice. Having died and revived again, one cannot be deceived;
with eyes empty of Buddhas and Patriarchs, even Zhang Guai is exposed. This reaches the point where Moshan folds his robes in respect and Tiemo hides his form.
His reputation spreads in all directions as he enters the Imperial Garden. Now that the timing and conditions have arrived, the true command must be executed. We hope you will grant your consent.
From [the Master]: "Do not be overly humble or self-effacing.
The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huaihai (Concluded).
At this time, the fourth year of the Bōei era, the text was collated against other editions using incense as an offering.
In the year of Dingshai, during the first ten days of the middle summer month, the bhikṣu Chujiang of Fengtai respectfully records this.
